data.title: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Is Ready to Halt Moscow Strikes Until Monday
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he had spoken with a representative of U.S. President Donald Trump and that from that day until Monday, September 7, Ukraine was willing to stop attacks on Moscow and hoped Russia would also stop attacks on Kyiv. He said a diplomatic event planned for September 6 in Kyiv, with a U.S. team participating, had been finalized, and that the Ukrainian side was ready for substantive talks with U.S. presidential envoy Witkoff and Kushner.

data.title: Putin Meets Witkoff and Kushner for More Than 3 Hours, Ushakov Says
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Russian President Vladimir Putin met with U.S. President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner at the Kremlin for more than three hours on the evening of December 5, and the talks were described as substantive, constructive, extremely frank, and based on mutual trust.

data.title: U.S.-Iran Military Conflict Continues as Both Sides Report Attacks on Tankers
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S.-Iran military conflict continued on the 5th, with the U.S. saying it struck three Iranian tankers, while Iran said U.S. forces attacked three Iranian tankers out of desperation over the Strait of Hormuz being blocked and caused damage.

data.title: Base Co-Founder Jesse Pollak Says X Account Was Hacked and Used to Promote Scam Token
data.description:
Base co-founder Jesse Pollak said on X that his account was hacked and that the attacker used a third-party app connected to the account to post a scam token ticker. According to Odaily, Pollak said the posts have been deleted, all third-party app connections have been removed, and he has fully regained control of the account.

Screenshots of the deleted post showed the attacker promoted a token called BASEMEME and described it as the "first meme coin with real utility," while also including an o1.exchange trading link and contract address. The meme coin's market value is now $257,000.

data.title: Counterpoint: Global DRAM Market Revenue Jumps 385% in Q2 2026; CXMT Share Rises to 10%
data.description: Counterpoint Research said global DRAM market revenue rose 385% year on year and 57% quarter on quarter in the second quarter of 2026, according to Jiemian News. Samsung Electronics held a 38% share of the market, SK Hynix 25% and Micron 24%, while CXMT's revenue share climbed to 10%, up 4 percentage points from a year earlier and 2 points from the previous quarter, ranking fourth.

data.title: Hyperliquid Policy Center CEO Says Meme Coin Regulation Could Become a Major Crypto Policy Issue
data.description: Hyperliquid Policy Center Chief Executive Jake Chervinsky said policymakers did not focus on meme coin regulation in the last cycle because many viewed them as a short-lived trend, and trading volumes later fell sharply. According to Odaily, he said meme coins could become an important regulatory issue in crypto policy if they grow again on a large scale and enter the mainstream market.

data.title: Israel Plans Partial Withdrawal From Southern Lebanon, Smaller Border Security Zone
data.description:
Israel is preparing to partially withdraw from southern Lebanon and establish a smaller security zone along the Israel-Lebanon border, according to Jiemian News. Israeli security officials said the planned deployment would pull troops back closer to the border, reducing the depth of the area under Israeli control in southern Lebanon from about 10 kilometers to 3 to 4 kilometers.

The new line is to be called the “Gray Line” and would replace the current “Yellow Line.” The plan still needs approval from the Israeli government. Under the proposal, the military would build new outposts inside the reduced security zone and use them as a base for operations to protect communities in northern Israel. Jiemian News also reported that the Israeli military is preparing for a possible escalation on the northern front and is guarding against potential responses from Hezbollah and Iran.

data.title: Odesa To Vote On Ban On Russian-Language Arts Content
data.description:
According to the BBC, Ukraine's third-biggest city, Odesa, will decide this week whether to support a controversial plan to ban Russian-language content in the arts. The proposal would add to existing national restrictions on Russian and would bar Russian-language music and literature, as well as its use in streets, parks, public institutions and state-run arts and entertainment venues; it would also recommend a ban in privately owned spaces.

The plan has drawn strong reactions in Odesa, where Russian is widely spoken, even though Ukrainian remains the only state language. Supporters say Russian-language content is used to weaken Ukrainian identity, while critics argue the move would pressure Russian-speakers and limit freedom of speech. The proposal is similar to measures already in force in Kyiv and some other cities, and its backers say it could influence private businesses even without formal penalties.

data.title: Climate Change Could Raise Airline Costs As Storm Disruptions Grow
data.description:
According to the BBC, airlines, airports and passengers could face higher costs and more frequent disruption as climate change makes severe weather more common and harder to manage. The article said thunderstorms, flooding, clear-air turbulence and rising sea levels are all posing growing risks to aviation, with some industry figures warning that busy airports in London and northern Europe are especially exposed.

The BBC reported that about 900 flights to and from Heathrow and Gatwick were delayed in late June after storms congested airspace, while dozens more were cancelled. Tim Atkinson, an airline risk consultant and former pilot, said there is a risk that storms could affect all of London’s airports at once, creating serious disruption and potentially dangerous fuel shortages. Former airline executive Andrew Charlton said the risk was low, but added that airlines may need to carry more fuel if storm-related diversions become more common, which would raise costs for passengers.

The article said Heathrow and Gatwick have already changed their landing-spacing systems to help reduce delays in high winds, while Gatwick has spent tens of millions of pounds on flood mitigation and expects to invest more than £2bn in expansion. It also cited research from Newcastle University saying 269 airports are already at risk of flooding from rising sea levels, with the total expected to rise, and said protecting airports could cost up to $57bn. The BBC also noted that clear-air turbulence is becoming more common, with Prof Paul Williams of the University of Reading saying severe turbulence on many busy routes could double, treble or worsen.

data.title: Tokenized Stock Weekly Trading Volume Nears $3 Billion in August
data.description:
Tokenized stock weekly trading volume reached nearly $3 billion in August, with Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, and Solana handling most of the activity. According to Odaily, the total value locked in on-chain tokenized stocks has exceeded $110 million, while only about 5% has been deployed in on-chain financial applications.

Grayscale said the tokenized stock market is still driven mainly by trading. On Solana, the size of related assets on lending platform Kamino and Jupiter has grown about 10 times from a year earlier, with lending and collateral use cases continuing to expand.

BNB Chain's cumulative tokenized stock trading volume exceeded $5.2 billion by the end of June, and more than 700 tokenized stocks and ETFs are available on the network. Solana recorded $5.77 billion in tokenized asset trading volume in the second quarter, including $4.8 billion in tokenized stock trading, about four times higher than in the first quarter.

data.title: Vitalik Says Ethereum Transaction Research Clarifies Actions and Dependencies
data.description:
Vitalik said recent research on transaction formats has given Ethereum a clearer understanding of the “actions” and “dependencies” in transactions, which can be optimized separately. According to Odaily, he said signatures, Merkle proofs for UTXOs, and ZK-SNARKs or STARKs fall under dependencies, while the call that sends ETH is an action.

He said dependencies can be processed in parallel, state-related dependencies can be handled by the mempool, and pure dependencies can be processed once at the mempool layer and may be replaced by STARK proofs to reduce execution and data processing. Vitalik also said Ethereum’s current scaling strategy needs to distinguish between dynamic, flexible parts and parts that can be statically analyzed, with the latter eligible for lower gas costs. He added that more than 90% of Ethereum activity by transaction volume does not require dynamic flexibility.

Vitalik said the EIP-8141 transaction type is moving toward a general, minimal call-list direction, and that new state types, recursive STARK mempools, and keyed nonces also fit that direction.

data.title: SEC Seeks Court Order to Force ISS to Turn Over Voting Data
data.description: According to Sina Finance, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission asked a federal court to order Institutional Shareholder Services to provide detailed client-level voting data needed for an investigation into the proxy voting adviser. The SEC said ISS refused to fully comply with an administrative subpoena and is seeking records from the past four years, including client identification documents and voting data. The investigation began in March to determine whether the company complied with securities laws, including its fiduciary duty to act in clients' best interests. In a filing on Friday, the SEC said it has full authority to examine whether ISS's proxy voting advice to clients was driven by specific political or policy goals that harmed client interests. The probe stems from an executive order signed by U.S. President Donald Trump in December last year, which directed the SEC chair to restrain proxy advisers such as ISS and Glass Lewis from giving guidance on diversity, equity and inclusion policies and environmental, social and governance matters.

data.title: Brazil Court Halts Sigma Lithium Mine Over Indigenous Land Dispute
data.description: A Brazilian court ordered the suspension of all environmental permits held by Sigma Lithium's operating subsidiary, Sigma Mineração, and required the company to fully stop mining at its Grota do Cirilo lithium project. According to Sina Finance, the Minas Gerais Quilombola Communities Federation sought the emergency injunction, accusing the miner of overstating the distance between the project and the traditional territory of the Baú Quilombola Indigenous community. The company said its Grota do Cirilo mine, located in the area known as Brazil's "Lithium Valley," is one of the world's largest hard-rock lithium deposits and includes a processing plant.
